subject: CardFlow performance follow-up: TTFT targets, burst throughput & streaming transport

Subject: CardFlow performance follow-up: TTFT targets, burst throughput & streaming transport

Hi Leah —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can size a short pilot:

Recap from our discussion
- Primary UX requirement: near-instant first token to keep checkout progress feeling snappy for users on mobile. Target we heard was ~200–300ms perceived.
- Typical output: short confirmation messages and 1–3 inline suggestions (average ~90–150 tokens per response).
- Expected concurrency at launch: steady 30 concurrent users during peak with burst up to 200 simultaneous requests for promotions.
- Acceptable p95 TTFT: <= 800ms during bursts; aspirational p50 TTFT: <= 250ms.
- Transport preference: SSE preferred for simpler reconnection/HTTP-friendly infra, but WebSocket acceptable for multiplexing many short-lived streams.

Questions / proposed pilot config (we can iterate):
1) Pilot traffic window: 48 hours of synthetic-level and traffic-shaped tests (we'll coordinate times).
2) Target config for pilot: aim for 250ms p50 TTFT, p95 <= 700ms under a 200 rps burst with 3x token caching enabled.
3) Concurrency plan: provision capacity for sustained 30 concurrent + 200 burst; if you want we can run a knob sweep to show cost/latency tradeoffs.
4) Streaming mode: we can run two short runs — SSE path and WebSocket path — to validate chunk cadence and reconnection behavior. We'll instrument per-chunk latency and packet sizes.

Attached is a short probe runbook and steps for capturing traces from your side. Can you confirm the following so we can schedule the pilot?
- A preferred 48 hour window next week (we suggested Wed/Thu).
- Which transport you'd prefer we test first (SSE or WebSocket).
- Any rate-limiting or gateway timeouts we should be aware of (CloudFront/LB idle timeouts, API Gateway configs, etc.).

I'll loop in Marissa and Priyom to scope the runbook and pilot parameters. If that looks good I'll send a calendar invite with the kickoff and a short tech pre-call.

Best,
David Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

David —

Thanks for the clear recap. This matches our internal notes. A few clarifications from our side:
- The 200–300ms perceived target is what product wants on average (p50). We understand p95 will be higher during bursts; we were hoping p95 could stay under 900ms.
- Average tokens will skew toward the lower end (we're seeing ~75 tokens median), but promotions will sometimes push responses to ~200 tokens.
- We're on AWS + CloudFront in front of our app. Idle LB timeout is 60s currently. No API gateway in front of the Redwood calls.

For the pilot: Wed/Thu next week looks good — can we do Wednesday (June 16) to get the infra team lined up?
For transport: let's test SSE first (simpler), then WebSocket if SSE shows issues with reconnection/ordering.

Tom will be the engineering lead on our side and will coordinate testing windows and provide access to a short load script.

—Leah

Leah —

Great — I'll put together a concise pilot runbook. A few items I'll include so both sides are ready:
- Test phases: baseline (low QPS, validate correctness), steady-state (30 concurrent at expected request mix), burst (200 rps for 5–10 minute windows repeated across the 48h).
- Measurement points: p50/p95 TTFT, per-chunk latency distribution, tokens emitted per chunk, end-to-end wall time as measured by client, and server-side tokens/sec.
- Fallback policy: if p95 exceeds 900ms for more than two consecutive burst runs we'll automatically fall back to a smaller model variant and document cost delta.
- Telemetry hooks we'll ask you to enable: client-side timing header X-Client-Start (epoch ms) and a small trace id so we can join logs.

I'll draft the runbook and share it to the Drive link David included. Priyom — can you add a short note on quantization/latency tradeoffs and the specific kernel selection we recommend for CardFlow's token sizes?

Marissa

Subject: Re: CardFlow performance follow-up: TTFT targets, burst throughput & streaming transport

Quick note from performance/ML infra perspective:

- For CardFlow's expected token distribution (median ~75, long tail to ~200) we recommend starting with an int8 quantized variant on A10x or equivalent; that hits a good cost/latency sweet spot.
- Kernel choice: prioritize reduced kernel overhead for short sequences (smaller attention tiling). That reduces per-chunk latency even if it slightly increases GPU utilization.
- Chunk cadence: emit ~32–48 token chunks for SSE in early tests to reduce per-chunk latency variance; if you see too many small partial chunks we can bump cadence to 64 tokens.
- Warm KV cache policy: keep a short warm window (30s) for likely users and a cold window for long-tail. This reduces tail latency during short, repeated interactions.

I'll add these as recommendations in Marissa's runbook.

—Priyom
Sr. Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
